## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

*Samasūpakapaṭiggahaṇa* is the twenty-ninth training rule of the *Sekhiya* section in the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka. It governs the monastic etiquette of food reception, specifically regulating that curries or bean sauces are accepted in the correct proportion relative to rice. An English translation has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 Within the Pali tradition, direct parallels exist in the *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* (Sekhiya 29), the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* and *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (Sekhiya 29), and both the Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī *Parivāra* (Sekhiya 29). Across other early Buddhist schools, corresponding rules are found in the Tibetan Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya for monks and nuns (Sekhiya 42 and 43 respectively), the Chinese Dharmaguptaka Vinaya for monks and nuns (Sekhiya 28), and a Chinese translation associated with the Upāliparipṛcchā (Sekhiya 27).

All returned citations in the reference literature refer to verse 29 of the non-Buddhist philosophical treatise *Sāṅkhyakārikā* rather than this Vinaya rule.

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog data.*
